neet_bio_u05_t02_1.working: About 97% of O2 is carried by RBCs as oxyhaemoglobin. The remaining ~3% travels dissolved in plasma.

neet_bio_u05_t02_2.working: Vital capacity = TV + IRV + ERV = 500 + 2500 + 1000 = 4000 mL. RV is not included in vital capacity.

neet_bio_u05_t02_3.working: Oxyhaemoglobin formation is favoured by high pO2, low pCO2, low H+ and lower temperature, as in the alveoli.

neet_bio_u05_t02_4.working: CO2 is 20-25 times more soluble than O2. That higher solubility is why CO2 diffuses much faster for the same partial pressure difference, so R explains A.

neet_bio_u05_t02_5.working: I: alveolar pO2 of 104 mm Hg exceeds 40 mm Hg in deoxygenated blood, so O2 diffuses into the blood (correct). II: about 70% of CO2 is carried as bicarbonate, formed with the help of carbonic anhydrase (correct).
